title: feat: improve model pricing layout
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Moves the seven-day requests-per-pollen estimate into the aligned pricing ledger with a distinct approximate-value badge.
- Keeps variable-pricing selectors beside capabilities, standardizes unit columns, and adds complete sort directions for price, Name A–Z/Z–A, Publisher A–Z/Z–A, and Newest/Oldest.
- Vertically centers desktop model details; mobile cards always show pricing and match the desktop label order; model rows switch solely at the established 42rem container breakpoint, including on touch devices.
- Makes Community models visible locally: the migrated local D1 is empty, so development supplements local Gen models with the public community catalog while preserving local entries; staging and production are unchanged.
- Validated with Biome, UI package type checks/build/tests (8), relevant Enter suites (47 tests), exact 671/672px breakpoint checks, and desktop/mobile/Community visual checks.

gist.headline: The price tags learned alignment
gist.blurb: The model garden got a tidier ledger: prices, capabilities, and pollen estimates now sit where wandering eyes can find them. Mobile gets the same useful details, because small screens deserve nice things too.
gist.summary: Reworked the Enter model catalog pricing layout with aligned unit columns, a distinct approximate seven-day requests-per-Pollen badge, nearby variable-pricing selectors, complete sorting options, and consistently detailed desktop and mobile model cards.
gist.impact: People browsing models can compare pricing, publishers, recency, capabilities, and estimated Pollen usage more quickly, with rows switching to mobile cards only at the established 42rem breakpoint.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the model catalog as a cozy garden-market pricing ledger: neat rows of seed packets and flower pots labeled with model names, each with aligned Pollen price tags and small approximate-value badges. Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses and holding a clipboard, carefully straightens the ledger while a friendly CRT monitor robot happily sorts cards by name, publisher, newest, and price; show a small phone beside the desktop terminal displaying the same tidy cards.
gist.image_prompt: A cozy pixel art garden-market workspace where the cute Polli bee mascot—with yellow body, dark brown stripes, black antennae and oval eyes, pink rectangular cheek blushes, a happy smile, light blue translucent wings, and tiny librarian glasses—straightens a neat model-pricing ledger of flower-pot cards with aligned Pollen tags and a small "~7 DAYS" pixel badge; a chunky CRT monitor robot sorts cards beside a phone showing matching mobile cards, with code-plants and flowers around them. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, dark purple (#110518) outlines, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, nostalgic but beautiful.
